declared_deviations.what: no separate terminal Adj event is emitted
declared_deviations.why: spec §3 recomputes after every registration and the vendored P0 Harness does exactly that inside each registration event, but it exposes no public Adj emitter; the import writes through the registration API only and never forges a log line, so the terminal adjudication is the state after the last event

declared_deviations.what: imported FCL problem records use SpawnTrigger.SEED
declared_deviations.why: the vendored enum has no 'import' member; 'seed' is the only trigger that does not assert an in-graph derivation. The clean fix is an enum addition, requested rather than papered over

declared_deviations.what: research problems use SpawnTrigger.RESEARCH with empty criteria
declared_deviations.why: the vendored enum has the member and §12 is exactly this path, but the trigger is not part of the v1.3 enum text; criteria stay empty because no instantiated commitment id is a criterion

declared_deviations.what: document-local depends refs are dropped, not turned into dep edges
declared_deviations.why: at node granularity they would be dep self-loops, i.e. cycles; toposort rejects them and a self-loop asserts nothing the author declared

declared_deviations.what: a self-targeting objection mints no warrant
declared_deviations.why: a Dung self-attack means 'this argument is self-defeating', which is not what an intra-document caveat asserts; minting it would flip two labels for reasons that have nothing to do with the evidence

declared_deviations.what: an objection against a record this import reified as a warrant attacks that warrant's validity node, not the node artifact
declared_deviations.why: spec §1 closure: attackers of a validity node attack the warrant and every carrier of it, so criticism of a criticism keeps its force instead of collapsing into a plain edge onto the carrier

declared_deviations.what: the retargeting rule above has ONE exception: an objection against a criticism carried by the SAME artifact is not retargeted
declared_deviations.why: the §1 closure lifts an attack on a validity node onto every carrier of the warrant, and for an intra-document criticism of a criticism that carrier is the objector itself, so retargeting would mint a self-attack through the closure and make the artifact self-defeating - which is not what an author asserts by qualifying their own earlier objection. `objection.o4` against `o1`/`o2` is exactly this case; it is dropped, not retargeted, and counted under its own code so the loss is visible rather than silent

declared_deviations.what: an FCL `claim` record maps to no spec construct
declared_deviations.why: a claim asserts content without proposing a test, so it is neither an observation-valued commitment nor a criticism nor a problem; it survives in the artifact body and in the FCL-1 document artifact, and is reported here because `uptake_refs_unmapped` covers only the claims the author put in `uptake`

problems.description: I share a flat with two friends. We keep arguing about ordinary household chores. Sometimes we agree on who will do something, but later we disagree about what the agreement meant. Our work schedules change, and one friend has started avoiding the conversations. What should I do?
Unknown why the friend avoids the conversations — overload, conflict-aversion, disengagement, or quietly doing less and dodging accountability; each implies a different remedy.
Unknown whether one person is systematically doing more work; perceived unfairness commonly drives chore conflict but is not established here.

Undiscriminated cause: do this flat's disputes arise at agreement time, from underspecified content, or at execution time, from divergent standards for what counts as done? The account's remedy touches both but with different emphases — writing versus calibration — and no discriminating observation is proposed.

What event should flip deliberately absorbing unevenness into raising fairness openly — a duration, a ratio, a felt sense? Without a trigger, tolerance has no terminus and can drift into a stable unfair equilibrium.

What evidence discriminates between underspecification and standards-or-trust explanations? Proposed cheap discriminators: whether disputes recur over tasks that were written down, and whether the avoider re-engages under a different convener or after the user stops proposing.

Domain ownership — the strongest item on the rival's decoupling menu for divergent standards, since an owner both sets and meets the standard — inherits the account's own churn objection: a domain bound to an owner can fail the way a rota bound to days does when the owner's shifts explode, and swap-on-request reintroduces the micro-agreements it was meant to escape. If the menu is opened, domains need scheduled swap review; until then this is unresolved.

The cause of the friend's avoidance stays open by design: the revised entrance does not require resolving it, and the opt-in window plus totals review generate evidence about which disjunct holds. The reserved one-to-one remains available if the window shows nothing.

The framing contest — agreement failure versus over-coupling — is deliberately not settled now; the probe's dispute-location check is the agreed discriminator, and both frames converge on the same first moves once the repairs and entrance replacement are accepted.

New caveat introduced by the revised entrance: it assumes the non-avoidant third flatmate is approachable and not part of the problem — not co-avoiding, not the quiet under-contributor. If the step-zero conversation reveals otherwise, the entrance fails and the design falls back to reserved one-to-ones with each friend separately, with no shared artifact until one is secured. This assumption is untestable from the exposed description.

Provenance gap: the rival input (cited within the synthesis as response.2#r1-r7) is not among the artifacts exposed at this carry step, so the synthesis's dependencies on it — the convener-verdict conjecture behind the entrance's stand-down, the discriminating checks inside k6, the stand-down-first ordering rejected in j1, and the rivalry side of the framing contest in pB — cannot be re-verified from the exposed material and are carried on the synthesis's own report. A missing view says what can currently be seen, not what happened earlier: this blocks no current action, but it does block any future relitigation of j1 or pB, which should first re-expose the source.
Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#cm1): Process-first private conversation with the avoidant friend precedes any group-level proposal.
Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#cm2): Adopt an explicitly provisional, availability-keyed, written task system instead of a permanent rota.
Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#cm3): Pre-agree a no-blame miss rule as part of the trial.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/account#cm4): Treat goodwill as the protected resource: tolerate temporary unevenness while schedules are unstable, refuse silent score-keeping, and raise fairness openly if that is the real issue.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/rival#r5): Before proposing any system, the user tells both flatmates they are done managing the chore question, then asks each separately what outcome they want, explicitly including decoupling options: separate shelves and cooking, domain ownership with swappable authority over each domain's standard, cost-split paid cleaning, or a time-limited agreement to tolerate more mess.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/response#k2): Extend the no-blame miss rule to definitions of done themselves: a contested line is treated as the defect — rewritten together at the next check-in rather than adjudicated against past performance — and the trial is entered expecting recurring meta-disputes at done-lines, with a standing rewrite channel budgeted for them.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/response#k3): State a ledger-use rule: the shared record may be used only openly, at the standing review, by anyone; no private tallies. Raising fairness is routinized as a standing agenda item rather than left to individual accusation.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/response#k4): Make a totals review the standing first item of the pre-agreed revision meeting: claimed versus completed tasks per person, looked at together, without blame.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/response#k5): Replace the process-first one-to-one as the plan's entrance. New entrance: (i) talk first with the non-avoidant third flatmate — the available, easy conversation — to co-own the proposal and to hear whether they perceive a fairness problem; (ii) start the artifact asynchronously and opt-in: one person opens the shared list with this week's tasks, done-lines, claiming rule, no-blame and rewrite rules, and a review date, joinable without any meeting; (iii) include an explicit stand-down line ('I don't want to run this — rearrange it freely'), co-signed if the third flatmate agrees, de-centering the user as convener; (iv) reserve the one-to-one with the avoidant friend until after the opt-in window, where it can be informed by whatever the window showed.

Observation-valued commitment with no covering evidence (daily/mini_fcl/cycle01/carry#d2): Refine the record-use rule into two named uses. Operational use of the shared artifact — posting tasks with done-lines, claiming against actual shifts, marking completion, re-claiming misses, initiating line-rewrites — is open and continuous, handled at short check-ins as needed. Evaluative use — claimed-versus-completed totals, fairness, deciding the branch — is reserved for the dated standing review. No private tallies of either kind. Check-in frequency is set by the flatmates at proposal time; the standing review keeps the pre-agreed revision date.
